text:
Erin: Quick sanity check — I ran a small interconnect heatmap sweep on the 8xA100 racks (both SXM-FullMesh and PCIe-fed) with the new 13B quantized flow. Pasting raw notes below, want eyes on the p99 tail behavior we saw.
Tomas: Which quant/exec path? int8/fused or int8/vanilla?
Jin: int8 + fused-kernel path (ml-rt v1.4). Model is our 13B internal fork, seq_len=2048, steady-state KV-cache hit enabled. Workload: mixed small requests (b=1-4) and a few large batch jobs (b=32) to stress sharing.
Erin: baseline numbers?
Jin: SXM full-mesh: throughput ~28k tok/s, p50 ~12ms, p95 ~38ms, p99 ~120ms. PCIe top-of-rack: throughput ~14k tok/s, p50 ~22ms, p95 ~85ms, p99 ~260ms.
Tomas: Wow p99 double on PCIe. But any tail spikes correlated with cross-socket comms?
perf-bot: Trace attached (auto): nvlink_util spikes coincide with p99 on SXM; on PCIe the PCIe_util and memcpy stalls are the culprit. Timeline: 2026-03-19T18:12:xxZ.
Erin: I saw intermittent 60-80% nvlink_util on SXM during mixed small-batch traffic, then sudden short bursts of memcpy stalls when large batches start.
Jin: Reproduced locally. Hypothesis: kernel choice (fused vs standard matmul) toggles different comm patterns — fused does more cross-GPU prefetching causing NVLink congestion on bursty traffic.
Rosa (infra): Can you share the exact run env? kernel/runtime flags?
Jin: Pasted env below:
```
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
export ML_RT=ml-rt-v1.4
export REDWOOD_EXEC_PATH=/opt/redwood/bin/fused_exec
# runtime flags
--batching.dynamic=true --kv_cache.shared=true --quant=int8
```
Tomas: Did you try NUMA pinning (bind worker threads + memory to local socket)?
Jin: Yes. Two modes:
- unpinned (default): OS chooses CPU/GPU affinity
- pinned: pin python worker threads + allocator to same NUMA for each GPU (taskset + numactl for process groups)
Result: On PCIe, pinning reduced p99 from 260ms -> ~180ms and increased throughput ~10%. On SXM, pinning had minor wins on p95 but p99 slightly worse in a couple runs.
Erin: Interesting — suggests different bottlenecks. Maybe pinning prevents cross-socket DMA thrash on PCIe but on SXM it forces more concentrated NVLink flows causing hotspots.
perf-bot: Quick grep of traces shows NCCL tree depth increased during pinned runs on SXM. nvlink hop count rose ~1.4x.
Rosa (infra): Try toggling NCCL_COLLNET=0 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL to see effect. Also try enabling NCCL_SHM for intra-node when using fused kernels.
Tomas: Also test running smaller kernel variant (matmul tiling variant) — there are two kernels in ml-rt: kernel_v1 (prefetch-heavy) and kernel_v2 (streamlined). Use --kernel=kernel_v2 to reduce cross-GPU prefetch.
Jin: Ran quick A/B: kernel_v2 on SXM gave slightly lower peak throughput (~-6%) but p99 improved from 120ms -> 88ms. On PCIe kernel_v2 matched throughput and p99 improved to ~150ms.
Erin: Can you paste the tiny ascii heatmap we generated? even rough numbers help.
Jin: pasted 8x8 pairwise avg memcpy latency (us):
```
SXM (full mesh) memcpy_us heatmap:
[ 0   3.1 3.0 3.2 10.1 10.5 10.4 10.2 ]
[ 3.1 0   2.9 3.1 10.2 10.6 10.3 10.4 ]
...
PCIe (root complex) memcpy_us: first row to other socket ~45-65us
```
Erin: So PCIe cross-socket latency ~5-10x higher, explains throughput but not the large p99 variance after pinning.
Tomas: Next steps: 1) run cross-region copy of the same matrix on eu-west1 SXM racks; 2) sweep kernel_v1/v2 with pinning/no-pinning and collect per-gpu nvlink_util/pcie_util; 3) try NCCL env toggles suggested by Rosa.
Rosa (infra): I'll spin up a dedicated run queue with telemetry collection (nvlink counters, procfs, perf events) and ensure MPS disabled for these runs so we isolate behavior.
Jin: I'll schedule the sweep and attach consolidated charts. Expect initial run this afternoon. If we see consistent hotspotting on SXM only when fused kernels + pinning, we should default to kernel_v2 for bursty small-batch workloads.
Erin: Perfect. If anyone wants to grab the quick configs I used for pinning, paste here and I'll add to the runbook.
Tomas: quick pinning snippet (for reference):
```
# spawn 4 processes pinned to 2 sockets
numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 python -m redwood.runner --gpus 0,1
numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 python -m redwood.runner --gpus 2,3
# set CUDA env per process
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
```
